recent_posts.title: Format Swift with a Git Commit Hook
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to automatically format Swift code on every Git commit using swift-format and pre-commit hooks. The guide covers configuring swift-format with custom settings, creating a bash script that formats staged Swift files before committing, and installing the hook in your Git repository. The approach ensures consistent code formatting across your project without manual intervention.

recent_posts.title: SwiftUI Custom URL Schemes
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to implement custom URL scheme handlers for SwiftUI WebViews in iOS 26. The guide covers creating a URLSchemeHandler protocol implementation to load local resources, registering the handler with WebPage configuration, and displaying content through WebView. Includes practical examples of building a quotes app that loads HTML files from the app bundle using a custom 'quotes://' URL scheme.

recent_posts.title: Swift Default Value in String Interpolations
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.2 introduces a new default value parameter for string interpolation that allows developers to provide fallback strings for optional values without type constraints. This feature addresses the common problem of handling nil values in string interpolation, offering a cleaner alternative to nil-coalescing operators or String(describing:). However, the feature currently has limitations with localization as LocalizedStringKey doesn't support the default parameter.

recent_posts.title: Treating Warnings As Errors In Swift Packages
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.2 introduces fine-grained compiler warning controls for Swift Packages, allowing developers to treat specific diagnostic groups as errors or warnings. Previously available only in Xcode build settings, these controls can now be configured directly in Package.swift files using new swiftSettings like treatAllWarnings(as: .error) and treatWarning("group", as: .warning). The settings only apply when building packages directly, not as remote dependencies.

recent_posts.title: Swift Raw Identifiers
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.2 introduces raw identifiers, allowing developers to use backticks around identifier names to bypass normal naming restrictions. This feature enables using whitespace, mathematical symbols, or numbers at the start of identifiers. Two practical applications include creating more descriptive Swift Testing function names without duplication and defining enum cases that start with numbers, such as video frame rates.

recent_posts.title: Swift Observations AsyncSequence for State Changes
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.2 introduces the Observations type that allows streaming state changes from Observable objects as AsyncSequence. This enables automatic saving of app state whenever Observable properties change, replacing the previous approach of monitoring scene phase transitions. The feature is particularly useful for persisting navigation state and scene-specific settings across app launches using SceneStorage, providing a more reliable alternative to the ObservableObject pattern with Combine publishers.

recent_posts.title: Approachable Concurrency in Swift Packages
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.2 introduces Approachable Concurrency, which assumes code runs on the main thread by default and only moves to background threads when necessary. New Xcode 26 projects enable this automatically, while existing projects require build setting changes. Swift Packages need swift-tools-version 6.2 and specific swiftSettings configurations including defaultIsolation(MainActor.self) and upcoming feature flags. The feature is still in beta with some known issues around protocols like CodingKey that expect nonisolated behavior.

recent_posts.title: Adding Icon Composer icons to Xcode
recent_posts.summary: Xcode 26 introduces Icon Composer, a new tool for creating app icons using the Liquid Glass design system. Instead of manually adding icon variants to asset catalogs, developers can now drag a single .icon file into their Xcode project navigator. The tool allows importing SVG layers from design applications and applying backgrounds, effects, and styling within Icon Composer. However, alternate app icons still require manual export and addition to asset catalogs, limiting the tool's full potential.

recent_posts.title: WWDC 2025 Viewing Guide
recent_posts.summary: WWDC 2025 introduces major updates across Apple's development ecosystem, headlined by the new Liquid Glass design system and expanded Apple Intelligence capabilities. Swift 6.2 brings improved concurrency with single-threaded defaults and easier adoption paths. The new Foundation Models framework provides API access to Apple's on-device LLM for private AI integration. SwiftUI and UIKit receive significant updates to support the glass design aesthetic, while new tools like Icon Composer and enhanced Xcode coding assistants streamline development workflows. The update spans all Apple platforms with notable improvements to visionOS spatial computing, enhanced accessibility features, and expanded APIs for health, payments, and system services.

recent_posts.title: Syncing TipKit with CloudKit
recent_posts.summary: iOS 18 introduces CloudKit sync support for TipKit, allowing tip states to synchronize across user devices. The setup process involves adding iCloud and CloudKit capabilities in Xcode, creating a container identifier ending with '.tips', enabling background modes, and configuring the Tips datastore with CloudKit container options. Developers using Core Data with CloudKit should use separate containers to avoid conflicts, as NSPersistentCloudKitContainer defaults to the first iCloud container identifier in entitlements.
